ModelCharacter: The flagship of Beneteau's enclosed outboard Antares range: a 36'7" two-cabin weekender with twin outboards, opening salon/cockpit connection and genuine family-cruising accommodations while retaining practical side access from the helm.
DesignLineage: Introduced around 2020 as the large flagship of the modern Antares outboard range.
Uses twin outboards up to 300 hp each rather than diesel inboard propulsion.

ModelCharacter: The first-generation Cutwater 24 Coupe: a fully enclosed, trailerable 8'6"-beam outboard cruiser that compresses a private forward berth, mid-berth, galley and enclosed head into a genuinely small performance hull.
DesignLineage: Cutwater launched the original C-24 as part of Fluid Motion's expansion of the brand beyond its early diesel cruisers.
The C-24 C uses the brand's double-stepped planing hull and single Yamaha outboard rather than the diesel inboard architecture of the C-26/C-28.
Cutwater later evolved this family into the C-242 and current C-248 Coupe generations.
The separate C-24 CW and C-24 DC open-boat variants moved to Fluid Motion's Solara brand after the 2022 model year.
OwnershipCharacter: True highway-width trailering and outboard serviceability keep ownership comparatively accessible. The boat is systems-dense for its size, so access, battery condition, plumbing and trailer condition matter almost as much as the Yamaha itself.

Strengths: Compact cruiser with substantial accommodation and systems for its length
Good helm visibility and short-handed features
Strong factory documentation and shared Fluid Motion support ecosystem
Weaknesses: Very tight engine space surrounding the blocks, interior storage is limited for month-long trips.
CommonProblems: Bow and stern thruster battery relay overheating, stepped hull speed-seal wearing.
TypicalMission: Trailer-assisted multi-regional loop segments and versatile family weekend trips.
AvoidIf: You want minimal systems and simple low-speed displacement operation
You prioritize wide machinery spaces and easy service access above compact packaging
You require a traditional full-keel single-diesel trawler

ModelCharacter: The best-known early Cutwater diesel cruiser: an 8'6"-beam, shaft-drive pocket yacht with a Volvo D4, strong cruising accommodations and enough semi-planing performance to run well above traditional trawler speeds.
DesignLineage: The C-28 is the larger sister to the C-26 and shares the same early Cutwater diesel-cruiser design language.
Factory manuals document a 28'4" molded hull, 32'4" rigged LOA and single Volvo D4 diesel.
Later production offered Northwest and Luxury equipment packages without changing the core hull identity.
The model was discontinued as Cutwater shifted its smaller cruiser range toward newer outboard platforms.
OwnershipCharacter: A capable compact cruiser with efficient slow-speed operation and useful higher-speed capability, but engine-room access is tight. Volvo aftercooler/heat-exchanger history, thrusters, generator options and electrical upgrades can strongly affect ownership cost.

ModelCharacter: A wide-beam low-rise pilothouse trawler that prioritizes interior volume, visibility and protected cruising while keeping a relatively low profile and economical single-engine drivetrain.
DesignLineage: Evolution of Helmsman's earlier 38 Pilothouse.
The 38E revised the deck, cockpit cover, pilothouse roof drainage, forward-window styling and sound attenuation.

OwnershipCharacter: Comfortable and unusually spacious for the nominal length, with strong machinery access and protected decks. Wide beam and substantial systems make it more marina- and maintenance-intensive than the 31.

ModelCharacter: Mainship’s third-generation mainstream trawler: a larger, more polished development of the 350/390 idea with molded flybridge stairs, two staterooms, lower helm and a huge outdoor bridge. It remains an economical semi-displacement cruiser but feels substantially more like a modern cruising yacht.
DesignLineage: Introduced in 2003 as the next generation after the highly successful 350/390 family.
The design uses related semi-displacement/full-keel architecture but adds length, salon space and molded bridge access; it is not merely a 390 rebadge.
Renamed 41 Expedition for 2009 and 414 Trawler for 2010–2012 while remaining the same core model family.
A 2009 interior revision replaced the forward dinette arrangement with a larger salon sofa layout.
OwnershipCharacter: Excellent cruising utility for a couple, but firmly yacht-scale in systems, dockage and refit cost. Single-diesel examples retain propulsion simplicity and protected running gear; twin-engine examples increase maneuverability but also machinery burden. The large flybridge and hotel systems add maintenance beyond the earlier 34s.

Strengths: Traditional teak interior and practical flybridge-sedan layout

Weaknesses: Substantial fuel burn profile when operating on active plane speeds, heavy tracking sluggish in low-speed tight turns.
CommonProblems: Exhaust riser elbow scaling build-up, window tracking perimeter core moisture leaks.
TypicalMission: Long-range coastal exploration, multi-month loop tracking, and comfortable liveaboard living.

You prefer single-engine economy and simplicity
You want low-maintenance modern construction details
